problem: RGB-based ObjectNav/VSN policies trained in simulation suffer a large sim-to-real domain gap, and HM3D's built-in semantic sensor is not a true, consistent semantic segmentation (labels/colors differ across scenes).
motivation: Semantic segmentation maps of real and simulated scenes are closer than their RGB images, and semantic priors (e.g., sofa in living room) help exploration. So using segmentation as the main visual input should improve both sim performance and real-world transfer.
key_idea: Train an imitation-learned recurrent ObjectNav policy that takes semantic segmentation (optionally plus RGB) as visual input, using a newly built consistent-label HM3D semantic sensor (SemNav 1630 / 40 categories).
insight: Coarser 40-category (NYUv2) labels beat 1630 categories in every configuration (e.g. RGBS+DINO SR 76.2 vs 70), since fine labels are noisy and unnecessary. Adding segmentation lifts an RGB PirlNav baseline from 60.9 to 72.9+ SR, and noise-injection studies show performance depends on segmentation quality (SR 76.2 to 64.05 with combined noise); category misclassification and spurious patches hurt most, boundary noise least.
method: SemNav dataset: converts HM3D packed texture-based semantic annotations into a Habitat semantic sensor with globally consistent labels/colors; two versions, 1630 categories and 40 NYUv2 categories.
Visual encoder: segmentation mapped to RGB colors and processed by ResNet-50 (512-d), optionally DINO-initialized; RGBS variant uses two parallel ResNet-50s for RGB and segmentation.
Other inputs: goal category embedding (32-d), relative position and orientation (cos/sin) via linear layers (32-d each), previous action embedding.
Policy: concatenated features go to a 2-layer GRU (hidden 2048), then an MLP to logits over 6 discrete actions (turn left/right, move forward/backward, look up/down, stop), max 500 steps.
Training: behavior cloning on 77k human HM3D demonstrations (Habitat-Web) with negative log-likelihood; optional RL finetuning following PirlNav (SemNav-RGBS+DINO→RL).

Real-world deployment: TurtleBot 2 with Orbbec Astra RGB-D; ESANet (NYUv2-pretrained) produces the segmentation online; ROS4VSN integration; new SDS metric (successes / actions in successful trajectories).
Noise robustness study: injects category-misclassification, boundary and localized-patch noise into the 40-class sensor.

setting.backbone: ResNet-50 (x1 or x2, random or DINO init) + GRU + MLP, trained from scratch / DINO init; ESANet for real-world segmentation
setting.model_size: about 189-229 MB on GPU (OS 188.54 MB, RGBS 228.79 MB)
setting.training_data: 77k human demonstrations from HM3D (Habitat-Web) with new SemNav semantic sensors; optional RL finetuning
setting.observation: Egocentric semantic segmentation (and RGB for RGBS variants) + relative position/heading (GPS/compass-like) + previous action + target category
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: turn left/right, move forward/backward, stop (6 actions incl. look up/down)
setting.privileged: Ground-truth semantic segmentation from HM3D annotations in simulation (real world uses ESANet predictions)

numbers.backbone: ResNet-50 x2 (DINO init) + GRU, IL then RL
numbers.extra: GT semantic segmentation from SemNav 40 sensor; IL on 77k demos + RL finetuning
numbers.evidence: Table: Comparison with state-of-the-art, HM3D validation set

numbers.eval_set_note: 3 houses, 5 categories, one episode per category per house
numbers.backbone: ResNet-50 x2 (DINO) + GRU, IL+RL, ESANet segmentation

numbers_note: Real-world SR is 73.3% in the table but text says 73.7%. SR is on the SemNav validation set, which uses the HM3D val scenes.
results: With GT segmentation, SemNav-RGBS+DINO reaches 76.2 SR / 0.36 SPL and RL finetuning gives 77.75 / 0.40 on HM3D ObjectNav val, beating PirlNav IL→RL (70.4/0.34) and XGX (72.9/0.36) in SR, but FiLM-Nav (77.0 SR, 0.41 SPL) has better SPL. In the real world, PirlNav (RGB) got 0% in house 1 while SemNav reached 60%, and the RL model averaged 73.3% over three houses.
limitations: Depends on segmentation quality; performance drops with noise, and sim results use GT segmentation while real deployment uses an imperfect ESANet.
Segmentation adds latency (ESANet ~1.4 s on CPU) and the real-world evaluation is tiny (5 episodes per house), with the robot unable to climb stairs.
No social navigation; limited to domains with available segmentation datasets.
